newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eight-month French grain use in feed seen up 11pct.
newsitem.headline: Eight-month French grain use in feed seen up 11pct.

text.p: French cereals office ONIC will this week announce an 11 percent increase in cereals demand for compound animal feed in the first eight months of the season -- between July 1, 1996, and March 1 this year, grain industry sources said.
Estimates to be published on Wednesday will show the biggest rise for barley, up 35 percent from the same period a year earlier, the sources said.
Maize will come next with a year-on-year rise in France of 24 percent followed by soft or common wheat, up 3.4 percent.
The rate of increase for total cereals use up to March 1 is down slightly from 12 percent recorded in the first seven months of the July/June crop year, sources said.
Officials at the agency said they never comment on monthly demand estimates before publication. ONIC is due to release its April supply/demand figures on Wednesday at 1000 GMT.
Industry sources gave the following breakdown of cereals going into manufactured feed between July 1 and March 1 (figures in thousands of tonnes).
In its previous report in March, ONIC projected total cereals consumption in manufactured feed for the year to June 30 of 9.3 million tonnes.
Of this, it predicted 5.7 million tonnes would be soft wheat, 950,000 tonnes barley and 2.65 million tonnes maize.

In the 1995/96 campaign, similar cereals use reached 8.368 million tonnes, of which 5.584 million tonnes was soft wheat, 867,000 barley, 1.917 million maize and 300 tonnes was durum wheat normally used for for pasta production.
